title: Quiz: Formula Notation, Model Matrix, and Categorical Predictors

questions.text: What does model_matrix(data, y ~ x^2 + x) actually produce in R?
options: Two columns: one for x and one for x squared
Three columns: intercept, x, and x^2
Only one predictor column because ^ is a formula operator that collapses to just x
An error because ^ is not allowed in formulas
questions.explanation: In R formulas, ^ means 'crossing up to this degree', not exponentiation. y ~ x^2 + x is equivalent to y ~ x — it collapses to a single x column. Use I(x^2) for literal squaring.

questions.text: A factor variable with 5 levels is added to an lm() model. How many columns does it contribute to the model matrix (assuming the default intercept is present)?
questions.explanation: With k levels and an intercept, R creates k-1 dummy columns (one level becomes the reference group absorbed into the intercept). For 5 levels: 5-1 = 4 dummy columns.

questions.text: Under OLS with a categorical predictor, the predicted value for each category is exactly equal to the sample mean of that category in the training data.
questions.explanation: When x is categorical and there are no other predictors, OLS minimises SSR within each group independently — which is achieved by predicting the group mean. This is the equivalence between OLS and one-way ANOVA.

questions.text: In the formula y ~ x1 - 1, what is removed?
options: The interaction between the intercept and x1
questions.explanation: In R formula syntax, -1 removes the implicit intercept. The resulting model passes through the origin (y-intercept = 0). This is useful when theory requires the line to pass through zero.

questions.text: The lm() intercept for a model with categorical x is 1.15. A new category 'e' (not in the training data) is added. What would add_predictions() return for group 'e'?
options: 1.15 (the intercept, as if 'e' were the reference group)
NA, because 'e' was not seen during training
An error, because lm() cannot predict for unseen factor levels
0, because the dummy variable for 'e' is missing
questions.explanation: R will return an error (or NA with a warning) when predict() encounters a factor level that was not present in the training data. The model does not know how to encode an unseen level.
